findings.F1: In the falling agitated profile in folds B and C, the next day's give-back after an up day does not grow with the rise's size against the 30-day swing: 58.0 % of in-profile up days are followed by a fall, but the correlation between the rise's size and the next day's short-direction unusual move is -0.057 (Spearman -0.0005).
findings.F2: The give-back by the rise's size in 30-day swings is flat and ragged, with no hump. It is +0.95 % (t 1.86, 354 cases, 166 days) for rises up to 0.5 swing, +1.17 % (t 1.74, 163 cases) for 0.5 to 1, -0.48 % (t -0.62, 64 cases) for 1 to 1.5, +1.29 % (t 1.17, 37 cases) for 1.5 to 2, and +1.00 % (t 0.37, 18 cases) for 2 to 3. This matches step 5's failed supporting check: middling minus largest is -0.12 %, even though the main measure is +0.60 % with t 2.44.
findings.F3: The plan's own scale does not show the peak at one usual swing either. Up days with a forecast of -10 to -5 give back +1.18 % (t 2.58, 358 cases), while those at -5 to -2 give back +0.40 % (t 0.54) and those at -2 to 0 give back +0.44 % (t 0.63). On the plan's standardised rise, 0.5 to 1 gives +1.52 % (t 2.53), but 1 to 1.5 gives -0.02 % (t -0.02) and 1.5 to 2 gives +0.81 % (t 0.58).
findings.F4: The brief's multi-day version is no clearer.
findings.F5: No condition inside the profile concentrates a graded effect.
findings.F6: Off the theme, large in-profile down days (at or below -1 swing) are followed by a next-day rise: the short-direction unusual move is -3.00 % (t -2.37, 141 cases, 68 days), against -0.76 % (t -1.97, 821 cases) for the same days outside the profile. This is a fall, not a rise, so it is another situation.

no_ideas: The theme's effect is not in the data. In-profile up days are followed by a small give-back the next day, but it does not grow with the rise against the coin's usual swing, at one day or over several days, in any part of the data (F1 to F5). The brief names exactly this as the case where its theory is wrong, and the test already used every coin and fold available.
